rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrasting the one who fears with the most wretched implies the latter is heedless in delusion and pleasure, seeking no escape from misery.
rows.anchor: ومقابلة { من يخشى } ب { الأشقى } تؤذن بأن { الأشقى } من شأنه أن لا يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Fire the greatest heightens warning and threat; it means Hell.
rows.anchor: ووصف النار ب { الكبرى } للتهويل والإنذار والمراد بها جهنم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks a higher rank of torment: burning is intensified because sensation continues without relief through death.
rows.anchor: و ( ثم ) للتراخي الرتبي تدل على أن معطوفها متراخي الرتبة في الغرض المسوق له الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not dying means not losing sensation; not living denies a pain-free life, preventing the audience from imagining a mild, nonfatal burning.
rows.anchor: فمعنى { لا يموت } : لا يزول عنه الإحساس ، فإن الموت فقدان الإحساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negations form antithesis, not a conventional denial of two qualities to establish an intermediate state; alternatively, denied life can imply no escape.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية محسن الطباق لأجل التضاد الظاهر بين { لا يموت } و { لا يحيى } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward passage is a rhetorical restart after the punishment, which was stated first as the main warning; the purified person is the same one who fears and remembers.
rows.anchor: فالمراد ب { من تزكى } هنا عين المراد ب ( من يخشى ويذكر ) فقد عرف هنا بأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falah gathers success and benefit: attaining the good one seeks.
rows.anchor: فإن الفلاح نجاح المرء فيما يطمح إليه فهو يجمع معنيي الفوز والنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense with qad presents success in the afterlife as certain, and encourages the wicked hearers to join those who feared and succeeded.
rows.anchor: والإتيان بفعل المضي في قوله أفلح } للتنبيه على المحقق وقوعه من الآخرة ، واقترانه بحرف { قد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakkā means striving to become pure through self-purification; the tafaʿʿul form indicates effort, beginning with monotheism and good Islamic works, including almsgiving.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { تزكى } : عالج أن يكون زكيا ، أي بذل استطاعته في تطهير نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet via Jabir explains purification as professing God's oneness, rejecting partners, and affirming the Prophet's mission.
rows.anchor: أخرج البزار عن جابر بن عبدالله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : { قد أفلح من تزكى } قال : من شهد أن لا إلاه إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, Ikrima, and Qatada identify the prayer as the five prescribed prayers, carefully maintained.
rows.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } قال : هي الصلوات الخمس والمحافظة عليها والاهتمام بها ، وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification comes first because it is the foundation of the subsequent work: a cleansed soul receives guidance and turns more readily to good.
rows.anchor: وقدم التزكي على ذكر الله والصلاة لأنه أصل العمل بذلك كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, remembering the Lord's name is spoken remembrance of God's names and exaltation, such as the testimony, takbir, and tasbih.
rows.anchor: وفعل { ذكر اسم ربه } يجوز أن يكون من الذكر اللساني الذي هو بكسر الذال فيكون كلمة { اسم ربه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhikr is inward recollection, with “name” pointing to God's character and attributes of perfection.
rows.anchor: من الذكر بضم الذال وهو حضور الشيء في النفس الذاكرة والمفكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer follows remembrance in either sense because remembering God prompts reverence and closeness through prayer, which combines submission and praise.
rows.anchor: وتفريع { فصلى } على { ذكر اسم ربه } على كلا الوجهين لأن الذكر بمعنييه يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three qualities unfold in order: purifying false beliefs, recalling God's perfection with fear and hope, then obeying and worshipping; prayer represents worship and leads to other deeds.
rows.anchor: وقد رتبت هذه الخصال الثلاث على الآية على ترتيب تولدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use second-person tuʾthirūn, addressing the polytheists with an abrupt shift; Abu Amr alone reads third-person, referring to the wretched who enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { تؤثرون } بمثناة فوقية بصيغة الخطاب ، والخطاب موجه للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal generally redirects discourse; with coordinated single words it cancels the preceding item, while with clauses it may cancel the claim or simply move to another report, as context determines.
rows.anchor: وحرف { بل } معناه الجامع هو الإضراب ، أي انصراف القول أو الحكم إلى ما يأتي بعد { بل } ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the afterlife is better and more lasting reinforces the rebuke: they have turned from considering what is superior and enduring.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { والآخرة خير وأبقى } عطف على جملة التوبيخ عطف الخبر على الإنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abqā is a comparative meaning longer in duration; a Prophetic garment report uses it similarly for what is more pious and lasting.
rows.anchor: و { أبقى } : اسم تفضيل ، أي أطول بقاء ، وفي حديث النهي عن جر الإزار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement dignifies this beneficial, enduring teaching as also found in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures, emphasized for deniers familiar with those messengers.
rows.anchor: تذييل للكلام وتنويه به بأنه من الكلام النافع الثابت في كتب إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” refers to the teaching from success through the afterlife's superiority; the earlier opening verses are not what the old scriptures confirm here.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بكلمة { هذا } إلى مجموع قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى إلى قوله وأبقى } ( الأعلى : 14 17 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and al-Ajurri report Abu Dharr asking the Prophet about revelation from Abraham's and Moses' scrolls; the Prophet recited 87:14–17, and Ibn Ashur could not establish the report's grade.
rows.anchor: روى ابن مردويه والآجري عن أبي ذر قال : ( قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان في صحف إبراهيم وموسى ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the scrolls” means that a counterpart in meaning is written there, using scrolls metonymically for their contents.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الظرفية من قوله : { لفي الصحف } أن مماثله في المعنى مكتوب في الصحف الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf is an irregular plural of ṣaḥīfa but the more eloquent form; Abraham had scrolls, while Moses had many, comprising the Torah's books.
rows.anchor: و { الصحف } : جمع صحيفة على غير قياس لأن قياس جمعه صحائف ، ولكنه مع كونه غير مقيس هو الأفصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording moves from a general mention to specification: “the scrolls of Abraham and Moses” apposes “the earlier scrolls.”
rows.anchor: وجاء نظم الكلام على أسلوب الإجمال والتفصيل ليكون لهذا الخبر مزيد تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common title is Surat al-Ghāshiyah, used in muṣḥafs and tafsirs and by al-Tirmidhi because the word opens the surah.
rows.anchor: سميت في المصاحف والتفاسير ( سورة الغاشية ) . وكذلك عنونها الترمذي في كتاب التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muwatta reports al-Dahhak ibn Qays asking al-Nuʿman ibn Bashir which surah the Prophet read alongside al-Jumuʿah; the answer “Hal atāka ḥadīth al-ghāshiyah” evidences this title, also used by al-Bukhari.
rows.anchor: وثبتت في السنة تسميتها ( هل أتاك حديث الغاشية ) ، ففي ( الموطأ ) أن الضحاك بن قيس سأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya shortens the title to Surat Hal Atāka.
rows.anchor: وربما سميت ( سورة هل أتاك ) بدون كلمة { حديث الغاشية } ، وبذلك عنونها ابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan by agreement, ranked sixty-seventh in revelation after al-Dhariyat and before al-Kahf, with twenty-six verses.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق . وهي معدودة السابعة والستين في عداد نزول السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah terrifies with the resurrection and contrasts punishment for the wretched with reward for the blessed, then rebukes people who ignore creation's evidence of God's oneness and capacity to resurrect.
rows.anchor: اشتملت هذه السورة على تهويل يوم القيامة وما فيه من عقاب قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its purposes also include strengthening the Prophet in his call despite rejection and warning that rejecters return to God for recompense.
rows.anchor: وتثبيتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الدعوة إلى الإسلام وأن لا يعبأ بإعراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question invites interest in the coming admonition; hal, which can convey “already,” heightens suspense by treating the important news as something the hearer should know.
rows.anchor: الافتتاح بالاستفهام عن بلوغ خبر الغاشية مستعمل في التشويق إلى معرفة هذا الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “come” can describe a report becoming widely known, as discussed in al-Naziʿat.
rows.anchor: وتقدم هنالك إطلاق فعل الإتيان على فشو الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the report as “the overwhelming” leaves its noun unstated to build suspense; hadith means either a report told or an event that occurred.
rows.anchor: وتعريف ما أضيف إليه حديث } بوصفه { الغاشية } الذي يقتضي موصوفا لم يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāshiyah derives from covering: it metaphorically names the Resurrection, whose terrors leave no escape and overwhelm the mind; it may alternatively derive from mental fainting.
rows.anchor: مشتقة من الغشيان وهو تغطية متمكنة وهي صفة أريد بها حادثة القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied noun is an event, with feminine form conventional in names for great occurrences; here Ghāshiyah has become the established name for the Hour, as “that day” confirms.
rows.anchor: و { الغاشية } هنا : علم بالغلبة على ساعة القيامة كما يؤذن بذلك قوله عقبه { وجوه يومئذ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Faces” is an indefinite subject of kind, with “humble,” “working,” and “weary” as three predicates describing people; the clause explains the event of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: { وجوه } مبتدأ و { خاشعة } خبر والجملة بيان لحديث الغاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces stand metonymically for their owners: the later pronoun treating them as rational people establishes this, and faces reveal their owners' joy or misery.
rows.anchor: فالوجوه كناية عن أصحابها ، إذ يكنى بالوجه عن الذات كقوله تعالى : { ويبقى وجه ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing humility, work, and exhaustion to faces may alternatively be a rational metaphor for attributing them to their owners.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل إسناد الخشوع والعمل والنصب إلى وجوه } من قبيل المجاز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm idh attaches to “humble” and is advanced for emphasis; the omitted clause after idh is supplied either from Ghāshiyah's sense or from context.
rows.anchor: ويتعلق { يومئذ } ب { خاشعة } قدم على متعلقه للاهتمام بذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashiʿah means humiliated, as in descriptions of the humbled on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: و { خاشعة } : ذليلة يطلق الخشوع على المذلة قال تعالى : { وتراهم يعرضون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Working” denotes being burdened with strenuous labor on that day, and nāṣibah means exhausted.
rows.anchor: والعاملة : المكلفة العمل من المشاق يومئذ . و { ناصبة } : من النصب وهو التعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptions allude to the damned: they neglected humility before God and labor in obedience, so their recompense is humiliating, exhausting work and hardship.
rows.anchor: وأوثر وصف { خاشعة } و { عاملة } و { ناصبة } تعريضا بأهل الشقاء بتذكيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Burns a scorching Fire” is a fourth predicate of the faces, or a circumstantial clause; naming the Fire after the verb heightens terror and supports its adjective.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { تصلى نارا حامية } خبر رابع عن { وجوه } . ويجوز أن تكون حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read taṣlā with fatḥah, meaning the Fire's heat reaches them; Abu Amr, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Yaqub read it with ḍamma as a causative passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تصلى } بفتح التاء أي يصيبها صلي النار . وقرأه أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective ḥāmiyah intensifies heat beyond its familiar degree, though heat is already intrinsic to fire.
rows.anchor: ووصف النار ب { حامية } لإفادة تجاوز حرها المقدار المعروف لأن الحمي من لوازم ماهية النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being given drink is a fifth predicate or circumstance; after burning, the listener expects a cooling drink, but theirs comes from a boiling spring.
rows.anchor: وأخبر عن { وجوه } خبرا خامسا بجملة { تسقى من عين آنية } أو هو حال من ضمير { تصلى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āniyah means heat at its extreme; the drink description also prompts the following account of their food.
rows.anchor: يقال : أنى إذا بلغ شدة الحرارة ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { يطوفون بينها وبين حميم آن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food clause is a sixth predicate or circumstance: it is painful punishment that nourishes no one and relieves no pain.
rows.anchor: أي يطعمون طعام إيلام وتعذيب لا نفع فيه لهم ولا يدفع عنهم ألما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍarīʿ is dried shibriq, a thorny plant poisonous when dry but grazed by camels and wild asses when fresh; Hell's food resembles it in foul taste and outcome.
rows.anchor: والضريع : يابس الشبرق ( بكسر الشين المعجمة وسكون الموحدة وكسر الراء ) وهو نبت ذو شوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes ḍarīʿ the Qur'an's name for a Hell tree that produces ghislin; min then marks origin, reconciling this passage with al-Haqqah.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضريع اسم سمى القرآن به شجرا في جهنم وأن هذا الشجر هو الذي يسيل منه الغسلين الوارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food neither fattens nor relieves hunger to show its pure harm; hunger itself may torment them, and eating ḍarīʿ leaves that pain unabated.
rows.anchor: ووصف ضريع بأنه لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع لتشويهه وأنه تمحض للضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saman means an animal's ample flesh and fat, while aghnā means to suffice or meet a need; min means “in place of” hunger.
rows.anchor: والإغناء : الإكفاء ودفع الحاجة . ومن جوع } متعلق ب { يغني } وحرف { من } لمعنى البدلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusive food clauses in al-Ghāshiyah and al-Haqqah support identifying ḍarīʿ as the Hell tree that yields ghislin.
rows.anchor: والقصر المستفاد من قوله : { ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع } مع قوله تعالى : { ولا طعام إلا من غسلين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed faces are separated from the preceding account as a fresh explanatory answer: after the warning is complete, the hearer wonders whether Resurrection has another, pleasant side for another people.
rows.anchor: جاءت الجملة بعدها مفصولة لأنها جعلت استئنافا بيانيا جوابا عن سؤال مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fresh statement functions as an inset that contrasts the two groups and turns warning to good news, following the Qur'anic pattern of alternating threat and encouragement.
rows.anchor: ولهذا النظم صارت هذه الجملة بمنزلة الاستطراد والتتميم ، لإظهار الفرق بين حالي الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the paired faces in ʿAbasa, these faces follow an opening ambiguity; the context identifies the first group as rejecters and this one as believers.
rows.anchor: وقد علم من سياق توجيه الخطاب إلى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الوجوه الأولى وجوه المكذبين بالرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāʿimah may derive from softness and beauty of appearance, or from possessing comfort, a good life, and luxury.
rows.anchor: و { ناعمة } : خبر عن { وجوه } . يجوز أن يكون مشتقا من نعم بضم العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “pleased with its striving” is a second predicate; striving means deeds done for benefit, and the believers approve their earthly obedience to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسعي : العمل الذي يسعاه المرء ليستفيد منه . وعبر به هنا مقابل قوله في ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In a lofty garden” is a third predicate; Garden may mean the whole abode of reward, comprising many gardens, or the generic class.
rows.anchor: والجنة أريد به مجموع دار الثواب الصادق بجنات كثيرة أو أريد به الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Height enhances beauty: elevated gardens offer pleasing views as well as lovely interiors.
rows.anchor: ووصف { جنة } ب { عالية } لزيادة الحسن لأن أحسن الجنات ما كان في المرتفعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lāghiyah is either a verbal noun meaning idle talk or an adjective for an implied utterance; calling words idle is a rational metaphor for their speakers' conduct.
rows.anchor: اللاغية : مصدر بمعنى اللغو مثل الكاذبة للكذب . والخائنة والعافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not hearing idle speech implies that none exists there; lāghw is useless talk, and Paradise is a realm of truth where purified souls speak only what ennobles them.
rows.anchor: ونفي سماع { لاغية } مكنى به عن انتفاء اللغو في الجنة من باب :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a second adjective of Garden; multiple adjectives or clauses may be joined or left unjoined, as authorities debate in examples from the Qur'an and Arabic.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { لا تسمع فيها لاغية } صفة ثانية ل { جنة } ( الغاشية : 10 ) ترك عطفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence gives Paradise's intrinsic height first, then its freedom from the defects of crowded human society; the verbal and nominal forms also favor separation.
rows.anchor: ابتدىء في تعداد صفات الجنة بصفتها الذاتية وهو كونها عالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This also praises Paradise through the goodness of its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وهذا وصف للجنة بحسن سكانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi reads passive feminine tasmaʿu with lāghiyah as its nominative subject; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ruways from Yaqub read passive masculine yusmaʿu with the same nominative, since the word is not truly feminine.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع { لا تسمع } بمثناة فوقية مضمومة و { لاغية } نائب فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Abu Jaafar, and Rawh from Yaqub read active tasmaʿa with lāghiyatan accusative, addressing an unspecified listener.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وروح عن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flowing spring is a third garden predicate and generic in reference, describing the gardens' complete beauty.
rows.anchor: صفة ثالثة ل { جنة } ( الغاشية : 10 ) . فالمراد جنس العيون كقوله تعالى : { علمت نفس ما أحضرت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spring clause is not joined to the preceding one because their verbal and nominal structures differ and one removes defects while the other asserts a blessing.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم تعطف على الجملة التي قبلهما لاختلافهما بالفعلية في الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised beds picture the garden's beauty even though elevation is already implicit in the idea of a couch.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الارتفاع عن الأرض مأخوذا في مفهوم السرر كان وصفها ب { مرفوعة } لتصوير حسنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beds are seats or couches large enough to recline on; raising them pictures their beauty although elevation is already part of the idea of a couch.
rows.anchor: و { سرر } : جمع سرير ، وهو ما يجلس عليه ويضطجع عليه فيسع الإنسان المضطجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cups are stemmed, handleless drinking vessels; their being set out signals that drink and its pleasure remain continually available.
rows.anchor: و { الأكواب } : جمع كوب بضم الكاف ، وهو إناء للخمر له ساق ولا عروة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between raised beds and cups placed at hand only suggests antithesis, since the literal senses oppose but the first is figurative.
rows.anchor: وبين { مرفوعة } و { موضوعة } ، إيهام الطباق لأن حقيقة معنى الرفع ضد حقيقة معنى الوضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namāriq are cushions for reclining, set in close rows so a sitter finds one wherever desired.
rows.anchor: والنمارق : جمع نمرقة بضم النون وسكون ميم بعدها راء مضمومة وهي الوسادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarābī are soft, colored wool rugs used for decoration and sitting in luxurious homes; the word traces to Azerbaijan, whose fleece and carpet craft were renowned.
rows.anchor: و { زرابي } : جمع زربية بفتح الزاي وسكون الراء وكسر الموحدة وتشديد الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for scattered rugs depicts their abundance across the floor.
rows.anchor: والمبثوثة : المنتشرة على الأرض بكثرة وذلك يفيد كناية عن الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's attributes answer the corresponding torments: humbling, exhausting work, burning, boiling drink, and hunger contrast with delight, a high garden, a flowing spring, and luxurious furnishings.
rows.anchor: وقد قوبلت صفات وجوه أهل النار بصفات وجوه أهل الجنة فقوبلت صفات { خاشعة } ( الغاشية : 2 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers receive familiar worldly forms of comfort, which console human spirits across eras and places, then gain blessings beyond anything seen, heard, or imagined.
rows.anchor: ولكن الأرواح ترتاح بمألوفاتها فتعطاها فيكون نعيم أرواح الناس في كل عصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the doomed are idolaters, the passage rebukes them for ignoring signs of oneness; the maker of vast creation can surely recreate the smaller human being after death.
rows.anchor: فرع على ذلك إنكار عليهم إعراضهم عن النظر في دلائل الوحدانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspoken subject of “do they look” is supplied by context; the rhetorical question condemns neglecting careful observation of God's works.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للاستفهام الإنكاري إنكارا عليهم إهمال النظر في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking means eye-sight that yields reflection, while “toward” directs attention more intently than a bare object; the comparison conveys focused attention.
rows.anchor: والنظر : نظر العين المفيد الاعتبار بدقائق المنظور ، وتعديته بحرف ( إلى ) تنبيه على إمعان النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “how” clauses are appositional complements of the named things, governed by the verb rather than the preposition; kayfa is an adverb of state.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { كيف خلقت } بدل اشتمال من الإبل والعامل فيه هو العامل في المبدل منه وهو فعل { ينظرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four objects are conspicuous in the intended Arabs' daily view, which makes them apt evidence for this audience.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت أشياء أربعة هي من الناظرين عن كثب لا تغيب عن أنظارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels sustain Arab livelihood as wealth, transport, food, clothing, and shelter; their strong legs, easy kneeling, and long powerful necks support heavy loads.
rows.anchor: فالإبل أموالهم ورواحلهم ، ومنها عيشهم ولباسهم ونسج بيوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stomachs store food and water, letting camels endure up to ten days of desert travel without drinking, unlike other animals.
rows.anchor: وجعل في بطونها أمعاء تختزن الطعام والماء بحيث تصبر على العطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camel features and journeys are celebrated throughout Arabic poetry, including the Muʿallaqāt and Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr's ode.
rows.anchor: وكم قد جرى ذكر الرواحل وصفاتها وحمدها في شعر العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative calls for continuing and persisting in reminder; its omitted object is supplied by the following statement that the Prophet is no controller over them.
rows.anchor: فالأمر مستعمل في طلب الاستمرار والدوام . ومفعول ( ذكر ) محذوف هو ضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innamā gives the reason for continuing despite inattention; its restriction reassures the Prophet that he must remind but is not responsible for producing their acceptance.
rows.anchor: والقصر المستفاد ب { إنما } قصر إضافي ، أي أنت مذكر لست وكيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You are not a coercer over them” is an appositional restatement of the restriction's negative side; muṣayṭir means one who compels.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لست عليهم بمصيطر } بدل اشتمال من جملة القصر باعتبار جانب النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is pronounced with ṣād by most readers, with sīn by Hisham, or with ṣād tinged by zāy by Hamza.
rows.anchor: والأشهر بالصاد . وتقدم في سورة الطور : { أم هم المصيطرون } وقرأ بها الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is reassurance rather than new information and is not abrogated by commands to fight; fighting followed a sequence of polytheist aggression and expulsion.
rows.anchor: فلا نسخ لحكم هذه الآية بآيات الأمر بقتالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects using the verse to establish religious freedom within the Muslim community: one who leaves Islam is given three days to repent, then killed, or ostracized and treated as a belligerent if unavailable.
rows.anchor: فمن يلحد في الإسلام بعد الدخول فيه يستتاب ثلاثا فإن لم يتب قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Over them” is fronted before its predicate to preserve the verse's cadence.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { عليهم } على متعلقه وهو ( مسيطر ) للرعاية على الفاصلة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception interrupts the reassurance to prevent rejecters from assuming they escape accountability; it is disconnected and means “but,” and the persistent disbeliever receives severe punishment.
rows.anchor: فحرف { إلا } للاستثناء المنقطع وهو بمعنى الاستدراك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result uses fa because the qualification is corrective and its general relative clause resembles a conditional; al-akbar figuratively means unusually strong.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء في الخبر وهو { فيعذبه الله } إذ كان الكلام استدراكا وكان المبتدأ موصولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return and reckoning explain why the Prophet need not force belief: God will judge them after their return to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: تعليل لجملة : { لست عليهم بمصيطر } ( الغاشية : 22 ) ، أي لست مكلفا بجبرهم على التذكر والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna here stresses and explains causation, although it does not answer an explicit denial.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء حرف { إن } على استعماله المشهور ، إذا جيء به لمجرد الاهتمام دون رد إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyāb means return to the place one left; resurrection is pictured as people returning to their creator, like a traveler returning home.
rows.anchor: والإياب : بتخفيف الياء الأوب ، أي الرجوع إلى المكان الذي صدر عنه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from third-person “God punishes” to first-person “to Us,” an instance of iltifāt.
rows.anchor: ونقل الكلام من أسلوب الغيبة في قوله : { فيعذبه الله } ( الغاشية : 24 ) إلى أسلوب التكلم بقوله : { إلينا } على طريقة الالتفات .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jaafar doubles the yāʾ in iyābahum; Ibn Jinni analyzes it as a verbal noun formed through a sound change and assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر { إيابهم } بتشديد الياء . فعن ابن جني هو مصدر على وزن فيعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks rank rather than mere time: reckoning is the purpose of return and a sharper threat for those who turn away.
rows.anchor: وعطفت جملة : { إن علينا حسابهم } بحرف { ثم } لإفادة التراخي الرتبي فإن حسابهم هو الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Upon Us” portrays their reckoning as a settled obligation in God's wisdom, as if God had imposed it upon Himself.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( على ) من قوله : { علينا حسابهم } أن حسابهم لتأكده في حكمة الله يشبه الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning is the main point for which the preceding return prepares; delayed punishment is respite, not escape.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة هي المقصود من التعليل التي قبلها بمعنى التمهيد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is consistently titled Surat al-Fajr; it is Meccan, though Ibn Atiyya transmits al-Dani's report that some called it Medinan.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية باتفاق سوى ما حكى ابن عطية عن أبي عمرو الداني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is tenth in revelation, after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
rows.anchor: وقد عدت العاشرة في عداد نزول السور . نزلت بعد سورة الليل وقبل سورة الضحى .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse counts vary: Medina and Mecca count thirty-two, including verses 15 and 16 as separate endings; Kufa and Syria count thirty, Basra twenty-nine, with different endpoints.
rows.anchor: وعدد آيها اثنتان وثلاثون عند أهل العدد بالمدينة ومكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah warns Meccan idolaters through the precedents of ʿAd, Thamud, and Pharaoh, announces the afterlife's punishment, and strengthens the Prophet with a promise that his enemies will pass away.
rows.anchor: حوت من الأغراض ضرب المثل لمشركي أهل مكة في إعراضهم عن قبول رسالة ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It refutes the belief that wealth proves God's favor and poverty His contempt, condemning failure to thank God, share with the vulnerable, and resist greed.
rows.anchor: وإبطال غرور المشركين من أهل مكة إذ يحسبون أن ما هم فيه من النعيم علامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It warns that people will regret not preparing useful deeds; wealth cannot benefit them then, while believers benefit through faith and entry into Paradise.
rows.anchor: وأنهم يندمون يوم القيامة على أن لم يقدموا لأنفسهم من الأعمال ما ينتفعون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fajr most likely means dawn generically, fitting its coordination with night; it may instead mean each day's dawn per Qatada, or the sacrifice-day dawn at Muzdalifah per Ibn Abbas, Ata, and Ikrima.
rows.anchor: فالتعريف في { الفجر } تعريف الجنس وهو الأظهر لمناسبة عطف { والليل إذا يسر } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are the known contiguous nights of Dhul-Hijjah; their indefinite form with a counted number conveys glorification, and no other annual ten nights match their sacred rites.
rows.anchor: وليس في ليالي السنة عشر ليال متتابعة عظيمة مثل عشر ذي الحجة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr identify the ten nights as those of Dhul-Hijjah, including the nights of Tarwiyah, Arafah, and the sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس وابن الزبير ، وروى أحمد والنسائي عن أبي الزبير ( المكي ) عن جابر بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet through Jabir ibn Abdullah says the ten are the ten days of sacrifice; Ibn al-Arabi judged it unsound, while Ibn Asakir found its transmitters acceptable but its attribution anomalous.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إن العشر عشر الأضحى ) قال ابن العربي : ولم يصح وقال ابن عساكر : رجاله لا بأس بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn ends the night, so their opposition unites the oath; the ten blessed nights are singled out as a subset of night.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة عطف { ليال عشر } على { الفجر } أن الفجر وقت انتهاء الليل ، فبينه وبين الليل جامع المضادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God originally appointed these nights in Abraham's law, but pre-Islamic intercalation displaced the lunar sacred months; its unknown start and scale prevent dating the original nights.
rows.anchor: وكانت الليالي العشر معينة من الله تعالى في شرع إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nights nevertheless existed during the year until revelation in the tenth year aligned the pilgrimage months with Abraham's calendar; the Prophet announced that time had returned to its created order.
rows.anchor: بأن أشهر الحج في تلك السنة وافقت ما كانت عليه السنة في عهد إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calendar displacement did not remove the blessing of the days on which pilgrimage rites occurred, since pilgrimage is worship devoted to God.
rows.anchor: وهذا التغيير لا يرفع بركة الأيام الجارية فيها المناسك قبل حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone assigns worship times; jurists call a time a legal “cause” meaning an indicator of the ruling, not its underlying divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: وتعيين الأوقات للعبادات مما انفرد الله به ، فلأوقات العبادات حرمات بالجعل الرباني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disruption of a divinely set time does not cancel the worship tied to it; the oath invokes nights whose exact identity is known to God.
rows.anchor: فقسم الله تعالى بالليالي العشر في هذه مما نزل بمكة قسم بما في علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One Prophetic report via Jabir calls the sacrifice day the even one and Arafah the odd one, focusing on these two days within the ten-night period.
rows.anchor: فعن جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الشفع يوم النحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Tirmidhi report from Imran ibn Husayn relates even and odd to prayer; Tirmidhi calls it rare, al-ʿĀriḍah notes an unknown transmitter, and Ibn Kathir prefers it as a Companion report.
rows.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) عن عمران بن حصين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( الشفع والوتر والصلاة منها شفع ومنها وتر ) . قال الترمذي : وهو حديث غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur recommends retaining both interpretations of even and odd.
rows.anchor: وينبغي حمل الآية على كلا التفسيرين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes even and odd the first two and third days after Mina, the counted days, outside the ten nights.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الشفع يومان بعد يوم منى ، والوتر اليوم الثالث وهي الأيام المعدودات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ten nights suggests a particular annual set, while the definite even and odd suggest a known pair from those nights.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { ليال } وتعريف { الشفع والوتر } مشير إلى أن الليالي العشر ليال معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi collected eighteen partly overlapping readings of even and odd, but most do not fit the verse's connection with the ten nights.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير { الشفع والوتر } أقوال ثمانية عشر وبعضها متداخل استقصاها القرطبي ، وأكثرها لا يحسن حمل الآية عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce watr with fatḥah, the Quraysh and Hijaz form; Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf use kasrah, the Tamim and Bakr form; both mean odd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { والوتر } بفتح الواو وهي لغة قريش وأهل الحجاز .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is joined to the ten nights as the broader category or to dawn by contrast; it is sworn by as a sign of divine power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: و { الليل } عطف على { ليالي عشر } عطف الأعم على الأخص أو عطف على { الفجر } بجامع التضاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasri means traveling through darkness, describing the night after much of it has passed; the image also appears in other verses.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يسري : يمضي سائرا في الظلام ، أي إذا انقضى منه جزء كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time of deep night allows people to sleep and then rise for night prayer.
rows.anchor: وتقييد { الليل } بظرف { إذا يسر } لأنه وقت تمكن ظلمة الليل فحينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, Abu Jaafar, and Yaqub pronounce the yāʾ in connection but omit it at pause for cadence; Abu Ali says final yāʾ may be dropped in a verse-end.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب : { إذا يسري } بياء بعد الراء في الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain the yāʾ both in connected reading and at pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب بثبوت الياء بعد الراء في الوصل وفي الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers omit yāʾ in both positions, matching the muṣḥaf spelling; those who retain it rely on oral transmission or understand the spelling as representing pause pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بدون ياء وصلا ووقفا ، وهذه الرواية يوافقها رسم المصحف إياها بدون ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The historical lessons either constitute evidence for an omitted oath-answer, or precede “Your Lord is indeed watching” to build suspense and prepare the audience for that answer.
rows.anchor: فهذه العبر جزئيات من مضمون جواب القسم ، فإن كان محذوفا فذكرها دليله ، وإن كان الجواب قوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did you not see?” may mean certain knowledge likened to sight because the stories are famous, or actual sight of the traces; kayfa is interrogative in the first reading and a noun in the second.
rows.anchor: والرؤية في { ألم تر } يجوز أن تكون رؤية علمية تشبيها للعلم اليقيني بالرؤية في الوضوح والانكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your Lord” rather than God's name evokes guardianship and support, while the possessive address honors the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لما في وصف رب من الإشعار بالولاية والتأييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAd and Thamud open the warning because they were familiar; Pharaoh follows because Arabs knew Moses' mission to him through the region's scriptural communities.
rows.anchor: وقد ابتدئت الموعظة بذكر عاد وثمود لشهرتهما بين المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAd unambiguously denotes the people, as another verse says; Iram is their ancestral namesake and an apposition specifying the first ʿAd.
rows.anchor: وأريد ب ( عاد ) الأمة لا محالة قال تعالى : { وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم } ( هود : 59 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram is diptote as a foreign proper name, the name of Iram son of Sam son of Noah, ancestor of ʿAd; this distinguishes the first ʿAd from another tribe said to live near Mecca.
rows.anchor: وإرم بكسر الهمزة وفتح الراء اسم إرم بن سام بن نوح وهو جد عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud is diptote as the name of a known people; masculine plural “who carved” treats the tribe as a people rather than using feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: ومنع { ثمود } من الصرف لأن المراد به الأمة المعروفة ، ووصف باسم الموصول لجمع المذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jābū means cut or carve: Thamud hollowed rocks for homes, as another verse says; some say they were humanity's first stone and marble carvers.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { جابوا } : قطعوا ، أي نحتوا الصخر واتخذوا فيه بيوتا كما قال تعالى : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣakhr means large stones; a wād is low land between two mountains and also a channel for much water, with forms ending in dāl or yāʾ.
rows.anchor: و { الصخر } : الحجارة العظيمة . والواد : اسم لأرض كائنة بين جبلين منخفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read the valley name without final yāʾ; Ibn Kathir and Yaqub keep it in both positions, while Warsh from Nafi keeps it only in connection, following cadence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بدون ياء . وقرأه ابن كثير ويعقوب بياء في آخره وصلا ووقفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley is the established home of Thamud, also called Wadi al-Qura and al-Hijr; it lies between Khaybar and Tayma on the Medina-to-Syria route and was later inhabited by Jews and Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: والواد : علم بالغلبة على منازل ثمود ، ويقال له : وادي القرى ، بإضافته إلى ( القرى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet campaigned there and conquered it in year seven; local Arabs accepted Islam and Jews made a tax agreement. The bāʾ means location.
rows.anchor: وكان غزاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفتحه سنة سبع فأسلم من فيه من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means both him and his people.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { فرعون } هو وقومه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “possessor of stakes” is that Pharaoh's kingdom included pyramids whose shape resembles a stake driven into the ground.
rows.anchor: ووصف { ذي الأوتاد } لأن مملكته كانت تحتوي على الأهرام التي بناها أسلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the stakes are a metaphor for firmness and power, as in “possessor of pillars.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الأوتاد مستعارا للتمكن والثبات
